deep.reconstruction:
Context: the page continues a manuscript headed 'Theorie der elliptischen Modulfunctionen von R. Dedekind'. It is a draft of Dedekind's 1877 letter to Borchardt (Crelle 83), not a text by Riemann. Riemann is only cited. Dedekind's convention is ω' ↦ (γ+δω)/(α+βω) with αδ−βγ=1, which corresponds to the matrix [[δ,γ],[β,α]] of trace α+δ.

(end of 3) Each image (ω) of the fundamental domain under a substitution is a circular-arc triangle.
- The centres of its arcs lie on the real axis; arcs may degenerate to straight lines.
- It has one cusp −α/β, which is equivalent to ∞ (the class of rationals); the cusp is ∞ if β=0.
- No irrational real number belongs to any such field.
- The fields accumulate in infinite number and decreasing size toward the real axis.
This is the standard tessellation of the upper half-plane H by SL2(Z) (PSL2(Z)).

4 (Hauptsatz). There is a function v = val(ω), the 'valence'. It is constant on equivalence classes and gives a bijection between classes in H∪Q∪{∞} and the full v-sphere. Proof sketch:
- The imaginary axis splits the fundamental domain F into two symmetric halves. Each half is a circular-arc triangle with vertices i (angle π/2), ρ (angle π/3) and ∞ (angle 0).
- Map one half conformally onto a half-plane of v. This is the Riemann mapping theorem, cited as 'Riemann, Grundlagen … Art. 21', the 1851 dissertation.
- Extend across the symmetry axis by reflection, so that mirror points go to complex-conjugate v. This is the Schwarz reflection principle, used implicitly.
- F then maps onto the whole v-plane. Boundary points identified by ω→ω+1 or ω→−1/ω get the same real v.
- Extending by invariance gives a continuous function on all of H.
- The three free real constants of a real Möbius change of v are fixed by v(ρ)=0, v(i)=1, v(∞)=∞. In modern terms v = J = j/1728, Klein's absolute invariant.

5. Programme: derive a third-order ODE for v by studying the inverse function ω(v). Its branches differ by substitutions ω ↦ (γ+δω)/(α+βω).
- If two different branches meet at a branch point where ω=τ, then τ is a fixed point: τ(α+βτ)=γ+δτ, i.e. βτ²+(α−δ)τ−γ=0.
- The discriminant is (α−δ)²+4βγ = (α+δ)²−4(αδ−βγ) = (α+δ)²−4.
- τ must lie in H or be rational (irrational reals are excluded), so (α+δ)²−4 ≤ 0. This gives three cases:
  - α+δ=0: elliptic of order 2, τ ~ i, branch point v=1.
  - α+δ=±1: elliptic of order 3, τ ~ ρ, branch point v=0.
  - α+δ=±2: parabolic, τ ~ ∞, branch point v=∞.
- The margin note says the identification of τ follows from the arithmetic of Z[i] and Z[ρ].
- [My fill-in] For rational τ with β≠0, the discriminant (α+δ)²−4 must be a perfect square k². From (t−k)(t+k)=4 this forces t=±2, k=0. If β=0, then α=δ=±1 and the trace is ±2.
- The next page derives the branching data (2, 3, ∞) and the Schwarzian equation (v,ω) = 8/(9v²) + 23/(36v) + 3/(4(1−v)²) + 23/(36(1−v)).
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. The fixed-point equation and the discriminant identity (α−δ)²+4βγ = (α+δ)²−4 are correct.
Unjustified as written, though correct: excluding the case where (α+δ)²−4 > 0 with rational τ requires the perfect-square argument (only trace ±2 works). The text compresses this into '≤0'.
The continuation of the map by reflection (Schwarz reflection principle) and the continuity across field boundaries are asserted rather than proved; this is standard for the period.

results.what: Tessellation of the upper half-plane by images of the modular fundamental domain; each tile has one rational cusp and the tiles accumulate at the real axis
results.modern_name: Modular tessellation / fundamental domain of SL2(Z)

results.what: Existence and uniqueness of the valence v=val(ω), normalized by v(ρ)=0, v(i)=1, v(∞)=∞, obtained by conformally mapping half of the fundamental domain onto a half-plane and reflecting
results.modern_name: Klein's absolute invariant J = j/1728 (Dedekind's valence); Riemann mapping theorem plus Schwarz reflection

results.what: Classification of fixed points of elements of SL2(Z) by trace: trace 0 gives points equivalent to i, trace ±1 gives points equivalent to ρ, trace ±2 gives cusps; hence the branch points v=1, 0, ∞
results.modern_name: Elliptic/parabolic classification of modular transformations by trace

deep.surprise_reason: The page is explicitly a draft of Dedekind's 1877 'Theorie der elliptischen Modulfunctionen' (letter to Borchardt), kept among Riemann's papers. The content is Dedekind's published material, with Riemann cited only for the mapping theorem. Nothing here is new or attributable to Riemann.

'jedes solche Feld enthält einen aequivalenten −α/β' — the image is hard to read here; the sense is that each field contains one point −α/β (its cusp) of the class of rational numbers.
